posts.title: On My Desk Now: A Long-Forgotten Ekphrastic Project
posts.description: I recognize myself as a young poet experimenting with the idea of a “sentenceless” poem, letting free association and the rhythm generated by line breaks, prepositional phrases, and other grammatical fragments create a feeling of coherent syntax and inevitability of meaning at the end.

posts.title: Learning To Love The Questions: What Do We Mean When We Say Poetry Can Change The World?
posts.description: A monk, however, is still male and that maleness is the boundary the speaker does not allow himself to cross, even as he recognizes his own the capacity for opening up to the greater “fullness” that might turn him into a woman.

posts.title: Pulling On The Threads Of Jewish Exceptionalism
posts.description: Regardless of what one thinks about Zionism, Jew-hatred is a phenomenon in its own right and ought, therefore, to be understood on its own terms.
